comment: I am writing to express my disapproval of the billboard tradeoff being discussed on Wednesday. Please forward this email appropriately if necessary. 1. Dark sky (a). The presentation dated 7/16/21 https://millcreek.us/DocumentCenter/View/2415/7-16-21 Electronic-Marquee- Sponsorship-for-Millcreek-Common?bidld= mentions the International Dark Sky Association (IDA) says electronic billboards may help reduce overall light pollution. However, those guidelines say the signs should be "switched off completely after 2300h/11pm (or 30 minutes after the close of business for on-premises signs, whichever is later), and remain off until one hour before sunrise." https://www.darksky.or@/wp- content/uploads/2019/10/EMC-Guidelines-IDA2019-l.l.pdf The memorandum of agreement found here https://millcreek.us/%endaCenter/ViewFile/Item/332?filelD=ll519 says only one of three billboards is going to be turned off at night. Not mentioning this in the presentation is deliberately misleading and if Millcreek isn't going to follow the IDA guidelines, they aren't creating dark skies or reducing light pollution. 2. Dark sky (b). The guidelines linked above say "IDA disagrees with the 2016 recommendation... that EMC compliance measurements should use illuminance (foot- candles or lux) instead ofluminance (candela per square meter)." It further states, "footcandle or lux meters, can also be used to derive an approximate measurement of luminance, yet are prone to bias from other sources of light" and "will subsequently require that the EMC owner/vendor be contacted to set a pure white screen for proper measurement." Yet the memorandum of agreement with Reagan says the illuminance level is measured in foot candles, which at best means they are using a less accurate method of measurement and at worst is continuing to ignore the guidelines they infer are being followed. 3. Static signs. The commons would be better served by static signs that list a webpage. I can't imagine very many people standing around staring at the billboard, waiting for all the ads to cycle through, when they could just type a current events webpage into their phones in less time and could check it in the future from home. 4. Light pollution. The signs might not currently be shining into anyone's homes, but with the constant development in the area, plus the long lease on these signs, it seems pretty likely these lights will eventually reduce the livability of someone's home or business. Millcreek City Council, Planning Commission and ALL concerned- I cannot express how strongly I am opposed to digital billboards anywhere in our city! It seems that our council is rushing to a decision about this possibility when indeed there are many options yet to be explored. I stand with the opinion of the planning commission that rushing through the process is not necessary and more public input needs to be allowed. Changing our guiding documents and ordinances also seems to be a step (or more) backwards and costly. I am seriously concerned about the direction the council is heading as regards the billboards in the Commons. According to attorney Gary Sackett, Mayor Silvestrini and his wife have clear conflicts of interest regarding these billboards. Anyone on the council, or in the administration, who has a relationship with Reagan Outdoor Advertising should recuse themselves from any type of dispute, vote or negotiation that involves dealings with said company. This is a no brainer in my opinion. I would like our council to consult with independent legal expert to discover a fair market value of the billboard(s) in question. In conclusion: Placing the equivalent of six giant digital flashing advertising billboards in our new Millcreek Commons is not my idea of CONNECTING TO NATURE. Perhaps we should change our motto to "Connecting SOME to Dollars". Please read this out loud at the September 15, 2021 meeting. Sincerely, Your constituent and neighbor, Nancy Trouse
